result.keywords: This article describes a SCADA-inspired water distribution testbed designed for cybersecurity and network performance research. The setup combines control traffic monitoring with congestion-aware anomaly detection, generating labeled traces from simulated attacks and transient link saturation events. The study evaluates several machine learning methods, including Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, Logistic Regression, Naïve Bayes, and KNN, to classify both intrusion patterns and abnormal transport behavior in real time. The resulting dataset supports comparative analysis of offline training and live deployment, and the testbed is intended to help researchers study the interaction between industrial control security and TCP congestion dynamics in operational environments.
result.title: Adaptive SCADA Congestion Anomaly Detection for Water Network Testbeds
